questions.question: Choose the correct sentence with the present perfect continuous tense.
options: She has been painting the house for two weeks.
She painted the house for two weeks.
She has painted the house for two weeks.
She is painting the house for two weeks.
questions.answer: She has been painting the house for two weeks.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the third conditional?
options: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I study harder, I will pass the exam.
If I had studied harder, I would pass the exam.
If I studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
questions.answer: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.

questions.question: Select the correct modal verb for giving advice.
options: You _____ do that exercise every day.
You must do that exercise every day.
You should do that exercise every day.
You can do that exercise every day.
questions.answer: You should do that exercise every day.

questions.question: Which option correctly completes the sentence with a gerund or infinitive?
options: I remember _____ the film yesterday.
I remember see the film yesterday.
I remember seeing the film yesterday.
I remember to see the film yesterday.
questions.answer: I remember seeing the film yesterday.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative form.
options: My brother is _____ than me.
My brother is taller than I.
My brother is taller than me.
My brother is taller than mine.
questions.answer: My brother is taller than me.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the word 'despite'?
options: Despite the rain, the match was played.
In spite of the rain, the match was played.
Although the rain, the match was played.
Even though the rain, the match was played.
questions.answer: Despite the rain, the match was played.

questions.question: Select the correct option to complete the sentence with a relative clause.
options: The man _____ car is red is my uncle.
The man, whose car is red, is my uncle.
The man, who car is red, is my uncle.
The man, that car is red, is my uncle.
questions.answer: The man, whose car is red, is my uncle.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the present perfect tense?
options: I haven't seen him since last year.
I didn't see him since last year.
I haven't seen him for last year.
I haven't seen him in last year.
questions.answer: I haven't seen him since last year.

questions.question: Choose the correct conditional sentence.
options: If it _____ tomorrow, we won't go.
If it rains tomorrow, we won't go.
If it will rain tomorrow, we won't go.
If it rained tomorrow, we won't go.
questions.answer: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go.

questions.question: Select the correct word to complete the sentence with appropriate vocabulary.
options: The discovery was so _____ that it changed the way we understand the universe.
The discovery was so amazing that it changed the way we understand the universe.
The discovery was so amazing that it changed the way we understand the universe.
The discovery was so astonishing that it changed the way we understand the universe.
The discovery was so surprising that it changed the way we understand the universe.
questions.answer: The discovery was so astonishing that it changed the way we understand the universe.
